title: Context menus
description: Context menus show actions relevant to what was right-clicked (or long-pressed): the menu is built from contributions filtered by context (file type, selection state, permissions). The architecture is contribution points + context keys — extensions add items with 'when' clauses. Menus must open fast (<100ms) and never show disabled-everything lists.
mechanism: Contribution registry: {id, title, when, group, order}. On open: evaluate 'when' against context -> filter -> sort by group/order -> render. Submenus for overflow.
demo:
# context menu: contributions filtered by 'when' clauses
items = [
    {'id': 'copy', 'title': 'Copy', 'when': 'hasSelection', 'group': 'edit'},
    {'id': 'run', 'title': 'Run file', 'when': 'isPythonFile', 'group': 'run'},
    {'id': 'del', 'title': 'Delete', 'when': 'isWritable', 'group': 'edit'},
]
ctx = {'hasSelection': True, 'isPythonFile': True, 'isWritable': False}

menu = [i for i in items if ctx.get(i['when'])]
menu.sort(key=lambda i: (i['group'], i['id']))
for i in menu:
    print('[%s] %s' % (i['group'], i['title']))
print('when-clauses filter; groups order; opens <100ms')

title: Floating toolbars
description: Floating toolbars appear near the selection with the most likely actions: text selection -> bold/italic/link; image -> crop/filter. They replace the trip to the main toolbar with a 50px journey. The toolbar follows the selection (reposition on scroll), dismisses on Esc or click-away, and never covers the selection itself — offset above or below.
mechanism: On selection change (debounced): compute anchor rect -> position toolbar (above/below, clamped to viewport) -> show relevant actions. Hide on selection collapse, scroll (reposition), Esc.
demo:
# floating toolbar: anchor to selection, clamp to viewport
def place(anchor, toolbar_h=36, gap=8, viewport_h=600):
    ax, ay, aw, ah = anchor
    y = ay - toolbar_h - gap       # prefer above
    if y < 0:
        y = ay + ah + gap          # flip below
    y = max(0, min(y, viewport_h - toolbar_h))
    return (ax, y)

print('selection at top -> toolbar', place((100, 10, 80, 20)), '(flipped below)')
print('selection mid-page -> toolbar', place((100, 300, 80, 20)), '(above)')
print('never covers the selection; Esc or click-away dismisses')

title: Selection actions
description: Selection actions derive from what is selected: the system inspects the selection (text? code? image? multiple?) and offers the valid operations. The mapping is type-driven — a registry from selection type to actions — with smart defaults (the most-used action prominent). Multi-selection enables batch actions; empty selection offers insertion actions.
mechanism: Selection -> type inference -> action registry lookup -> rank by usage. Batch actions for multi-select. Preview the action's effect where possible.

title: Progressive disclosure
description: Progressive disclosure keeps floating UI small: show the 3-5 most likely actions, tuck the rest behind 'more'. The ranking comes from usage data and context — the menu learns. The 'more' panel is one click away, not hidden: discoverability survives because the full set is reachable and the overflow is clearly marked.
mechanism: Rank actions by (context relevance x usage frequency); show top N; overflow into 'more'. Track usage to re-rank. Never hide destructive actions without confirmation.
algo: O(actions log actions) rank; top-N render.
demo:
# top-N by relevance x frequency; the rest behind 'more'
actions = [
    ('Bold', 0.9, 120), ('Italic', 0.8, 40), ('Link', 0.7, 90),
    ('Code', 0.5, 15), ('Strikethrough', 0.4, 5), ('Highlight', 0.6, 25),
]
ranked = sorted(actions, key=lambda a: a[1] * a[2], reverse=True)
N = 4
print('shown:', [a[0] for a in ranked[:N]])
print('more:', [a[0] for a in ranked[N:]], '(one click away, clearly marked)')
print('ranking learns from usage; destructive actions always confirm')

title: Smart suggestions
description: Smart suggestions predict the action before the menu opens: based on the selection content and history, the system pre-selects or highlights the likely choice ('translate this Spanish text?', 'format this pasted code?'). It is a classifier over (selection features, user history) -> action. Wrong predictions must be cheap to dismiss — the suggestion is a hint, never a commitment.
mechanism: Features: selection text, type, app context, history. Heuristics or small model -> ranked suggestions. UI: highlighted default + one-key accept. Dismissal is free.
algo: O(features) inference; heuristics often beat ML here.

title: Gesture triggers
description: Gestures trigger floating actions without menus: right-click drag, two-finger tap, hover with modifier. The gesture recognizer maps pointer sequences to actions; the mapping must be discoverable (show hints) and forgiving (undo). Touch and mouse need different gesture sets — design both, test both.
mechanism: Recognizer: pointer events -> gesture classification -> action. Timeout for disambiguation. Visual feedback during the gesture (trail, highlight).
demo:
# gesture classification: pointer path -> action
def classify(points):
    (x0, y0), (x1, y1) = points[0], points[-1]
    dx, dy = x1 - x0, y1 - y0
    if abs(dx) < 10 and abs(dy) < 10:
        return 'tap: select'
    if abs(dx) > abs(dy) * 2:
        return 'swipe horizontal: next/prev'
    if dy < -50:
        return 'swipe up: actions menu'
    return 'drag: move'

print(classify([(0, 0), (2, 1)]))
print(classify([(0, 100), (5, 20)]))
print(classify([(0, 0), (80, 5)]))
print('feedback during the gesture; undo after; different sets for touch/mouse')

title: Positioning algorithms
description: Floating UI positioning is constraint solving: prefer above the anchor, flip below if clipped, shift horizontally to stay in viewport, shrink if nothing fits. The algorithm tries placements in preference order and picks the first with acceptable clipping. For complex UIs (nested menus), each submenu positions relative to its parent item with the same solver, recursively.
mechanism: Candidate placements ranked; score = visible area - overlap penalties; pick best. Clamp to viewport; flip axis on overflow. Submenus recurse.

title: Accessibility of floating actions
description: Floating actions must work keyboard-first: the menu opens with a shortcut, arrows navigate, Enter activates, Esc dismisses and returns focus. Screen readers get proper roles (menu, menuitem), aria-expanded states, and announced position. Focus never gets lost — dismissing returns focus to the anchor. Touch targets are 44px minimum.
mechanism: Roving tabindex in the menu; focus trap while open; return focus on close. ARIA menu pattern. Shortcut to open without the mouse.
algo: O(items) navigation; the work is in the contract.
demo:
print('FLOATING MENU ACCESSIBILITY CONTRACT')
print('open: keyboard shortcut (not just right-click)')
print('navigate: arrows (roving tabindex); type-ahead jumps')
print('activate: Enter/Space; dismiss: Esc (focus RETURNS to anchor)')
print('SR: role=menu/menuitem, aria-expanded, position announced')
print('touch: 44px targets minimum')
print('focus is never lost: dismiss always restores the anchor')

title: Theming floating UI
description: Floating UI themes through the same token system as the app: surfaces, borders, shadows, and text colors come from tokens, so dark mode and high contrast apply automatically. Elevation is semantic (overlay level), not hardcoded shadows. The little arrow/caret inherits the surface color. Theme changes re-render open menus — no stale colors.
mechanism: Tokens: --overlay-bg, --overlay-border, --overlay-shadow. Elevation scale. Re-render on theme change events.
algo: O(1) token lookup; re-render on change.

title: Telemetry for floating actions
description: Telemetry tells which floating actions earn their place: open rate, action pick rate, time-to-pick, dismiss rate. High dismiss + low pick = the trigger is wrong or the actions are. The data re-ranks progressive disclosure and prunes dead actions. Privacy: aggregate counts, never selection contents.
mechanism: Events: menu_opened, action_picked, dismissed, time_to_pick. Aggregate by action; dashboards per surface. Never log the selected text.
algo: O(events) aggregation; privacy by never logging contents.

title: A/B testing actions
description: Floating action designs are A/B tested: which actions shown, their order, the trigger gesture. The test randomizes users into variants, measures pick rate and task completion, and ships the winner. Guardrails: no variant may hide destructive-action confirmations; accessibility variants are not tested away. Small surfaces, fast tests — floating UI iterates weekly.
mechanism: Feature flags per variant; metrics: pick rate, time-to-pick, task success. Minimum sample + significance before shipping. Kill switch per variant.
algo: O(users) assignment; stats on the metrics.
demo:
import random
random.seed(1)

# A/B: variant B shows 'Link' first. Metric: pick rate.
variants = {'A': 0.31, 'B': 0.38}  # true pick rates (unknown to us)
results = {}
for v, rate in variants.items():
    picks = sum(1 for _ in range(2000) if random.random() < rate)
    results[v] = picks / 2000
print('pick rate:', {v: '%.3f' % r for v, r in results.items()})
print('winner: B (+%.0f%% relative)' % ((results['B']/results['A'] - 1) * 100))
print('guardrails: confirmations never tested away; kill switch per variant')

title: Mobile floating patterns
description: Mobile floating actions differ: bottom sheets replace context menus (thumb reach), long-press replaces right-click, and actions are full-width rows, not tiny menu items. The trigger is usually selection + a floating handle, or a long-press. Haptics confirm the trigger. Test on real thumbs — the 44px minimum is a floor, not a target.
mechanism: Long-press (500ms) -> bottom sheet or floating bar; selection handles for adjust; haptic on trigger. Bottom sheet = the mobile context menu.
algo: O(1); the design is the work.

title: Performance of floating UI
description: Floating UI must feel instant: open in <100ms, reposition without jank, never block the main thread on show. The costs are layout (measure the anchor), render (build the menu), and positioning (the solver). Mitigations: pre-build the menu offscreen, cache measurements, use transform for moves (compositor-only), and virtualize long menus.
mechanism: Pre-build hidden; transform-based positioning; rAF-throttled reposition on scroll; virtualize >50 items. Measure open latency in CI.
algo: O(1) show via pre-build; transform moves are compositor-only.
demo:
print('FLOATING UI PERF BUDGET')
print('open: <100ms (pre-build the menu hidden; show = toggle)')
print('move: transform only (compositor thread, no layout)')
print('scroll: reposition on rAF throttle (not per event)')
print('long menus: virtualize past 50 items')
print('measure open latency in CI: budgets are tested, not hoped')

title: Plugin APIs for actions
description: Plugins contribute floating actions through the same menu API as built-ins: register items with when-clauses, groups, and icons. The host sandboxes untrusted contributions (no direct DOM, declarative items only). Versioning keeps old plugins working. The API is the product — VS Code's menus succeeded because the contribution model is simple and documented.
mechanism: Declarative contributions in the manifest; host evaluates when-clauses; commands as the action handlers. Icons themed. API versioned.

title: Floating action guidelines
description: The guidelines that keep floating actions humane: show fewer than 7 items; the most likely first; destructive actions separated and confirming; never cover the selection; dismiss easily; keyboard parity; consistent placement across the app. Guidelines are enforced by the shared component — not every team re-decides. Review new floating UI against the checklist.
mechanism: Shared FloatingActions component encoding the rules; design review checklist; telemetry verifying compliance (dismiss rates).
algo: O(1) — a checklist, enforced by the component.
demo:
print('FLOATING ACTION CHECKLIST')
for rule in [
    'fewer than 7 items (rest behind more)',
    'most likely action first (ranked, learning)',
    'destructive: separated + confirming',
    'never covers the selection (offset, flip)',
    'dismiss: Esc, click-away, focus returns to anchor',
    'keyboard parity: shortcut opens, arrows navigate',
    'consistent placement across the app (shared component)',
]:
    print(' [ ]', rule)
print('enforced by the shared component, not by hope')
